findings.title: Loop-round usage is omitted from run totals
findings.description: `StateManager` persists only `step_result.action_results`. The executor keeps earlier loop-round results separately in `StepResult.prior_rounds`, so those LLM calls are absent from persisted state. Since `run_usage_report` reads only persisted action results (`src/squadron/stats/usage_report.py:113-114`), a multi-round loop reports only its final round’s usage and undercounts the run.

findings.title: Fan-out branch usage is discarded before stats can report it
findings.description: The fan-out branches carry usage records on their action metadata, but `CollectReducer` copies only action type, success, outputs, and verdict into the returned result. `FirstPassReducer` likewise returns outputs and verdict without metadata. The persisted result therefore has no branch usage, and `sq stats run` cannot include those LLM calls in its totals.

findings.title: Split-review totals retain only the first part’s usage
findings.description: Each review part receives its own usage record, but `_metadata` starts from only `parts[0].metadata` and does not combine the usage records. For a split review, the folded action—and therefore run stats—counts only the first part’s spend.

findings.title: Compact calls can spend tokens without recording usage
findings.description: The prompt-only compact path calls `claude_agent_sdk.query()` and consumes messages only to find the compact boundary; it never reads or stamps result usage. In the SDK-session path, the broad exception handler at `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/compact.py:82-90` also returns a failed result without recording telemetry that may be attached to the provider error. Since compact is counted as an LLM action, these paths leave spend out of run stats.

findings.title: Malformed `costBasis` values can crash the reviews report
findings.description: `_basis` tests the parsed frontmatter value for membership in a set before validating its type. YAML can parse `costBasis` as a list or mapping, which is unhashable and raises `TypeError` instead of warning and treating the field as malformed. One such artifact can abort `sq stats reviews`.

findings.title: Review artifacts usually lose the alias needed to label subscription costs
findings.description: The reviews report determines an alias only from `requestedModel`. However, `format_review_markdown` writes `requestedModel` only when the answering model differs from the requested model (`src/squadron/review/persistence.py:608`). For the common case where the requested model answers, the alias is therefore `None`; subscription-tier provider costs cannot be labeled as API-rate equivalents and may be displayed as ordinary provider cost.
